shows.description:
Funky Corners returns for another Friday-night episode. We drop a West Coast hip hop set early in the show followed by instrumental beats, a touch of jazz/funk, and wrap things up with some East Coast rap & remixes.
 
For the Crate Highlight, we spin the original cut sampled for O.C.'s "Time's Up".

For the Crate Highlight, we drop the original beat used to make Big Daddy Kane's "Ain't No Half-Steppin'."

Other selections include: Slick Rick, The Goats, The Afros, 3rd Bass, Dexter Wansel, Lyn Collins, The Wild Magnolias, and Donald Byrd.

We reveal which B.T. Express song EPMD used for "So What Cha Sayin’" in the Crate Highlight segment.
 
Other selections include: Diamond D, Chi-Ali, Lords of the Underground, Gil-Scott Heron, The Liquid Crystal Project, Ronnie Laws, and Johnny Madwreck.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #40 08-11-2012
shows.description:
Fresh from the Orient, Kid Taiwan joins us for a most memorable Funky Corners. The show commences with a beatbox/freestyle session between The Kid & Raider’s Hat then it’s all downhill from there. Kid Taiwan brings a few choice tracks and gives us his opinion on the state of breakdancing in Taiwan.
 
For the Crate Highlight, we drop “Between The Sheets” by the Isley Brothers and show you who sampled it the best.
 
Other selections include: KRS-One, Trilogy, Main Source, Dr. Octagon, Ohio Players, Galt MacDermot, and Villain Accelerate.
tracks: Dr. Hellno And The Praying Mantus
Blue Flowers (Prince Paul’s So So Beautiful Mix)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #41 08-19-2012
shows.description:
We keep it up-tempo in show #41 with bouncy hip hop and a load of b-boy/breaking tracks.
 
In the Crate Highlight segment, find out which early hip hop track used “Cavern” by Liquid Liquid in 1983.
 
Other selections include: Intelligent Hoodlum, Fu-Schnickens, The Dismasters, Banda Black Rio, The Last Poets, and a rarely-heard Michael Jackson home demo.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #42 08-25-2012
shows.description:
We do it up funky potpourri style on show #42, blending that hip hop, beats, funk and ragga dancehall. We also talk about what makes the returning students special at SUNY Albany. 

We drop some tracks that sampled Betty Wright’s “Clean Up Woman”, in the Crate Highlight portion of the show.

Selections also include: DJ Wally, Black Star, OC, Love Unlimited, The Meters, Mad Lion, and Cutty Ranks.
tracks: A Who She Me Dun (Dynamik Duo Remix)
Day’s End (After-Dusk Mix Feat. Kazufumi Kodama)

shows.description:

Find out which J.B.’s track EPMD, Nas and J-Live all sampled in this episode’s Crate Highlight.
 
Other selections include: Quasimoto, Willowy, Dayton Sidewinders, Oscar Brown Jr., Ice-T, Lord Finesse, Pudgee Tha Phat Bastard, Saul Williams, and a most profound white rapper version of “C.R.E.A.M.”

Upon its release, Show #44 was our most up-tempo program, consisting of electro, funk & hip hop at 120+ BPM. 

We link up Pete Rock & C.L. Smooth with Eddie Bo in the Crate Highlight segment.

Other selections include: Afrika Bambaata, George Kranz, Newcleus, Crooklyn Dodgers (both sets), Kid Capri, Royal Flush, Ursula 1000, and Herman Kelly.

shows.description:

It’s the last day of summer so we do up the Crate Highlight with perennial BBQ classic “Nuthin’ But A G Thang.”

Other selections include: Al Green, Big L, The D.O.C., Gang Starr, Lords Of The Underground and Little People.

shows.description:
Beats, funk, hip hop and dancehall all get spun together for a well-balanced Show #47. 

We play you the original beat used to make K-Solo’s “Your Mom’s In My Business” in the Crate Highlight segment.

Other selections include: Craig G, Fat Joe, Too $hort, Kool & The Gang, Curtis Mayfield, Peace Orchestra, Nightmares On Wax and a Public Enemy extended mix.

shows.description:
It’s Funky Corners’ one-year anniversary! To mark the occasion, we play nothing but vinyl. D.A. Jay & Fatty join us for a little freestyle action and other shenanigans.

We pull a Crate Highlight 45, spotlighting “I Get Lifted” by George McCrae.

Other selections include: Average White Band, Bobbi Humphrey, Capleton, Rayvon, Whitey Don, Craig Mack, D&D All-Stars, Professor Griff and the Pig Food Records crew.

shows.description:
Fatty rejoins us in the studio for Funky Corners #49. We start the show off a little more electronic-esque than usual, but soon after kick into the rapty-rap. The second half features a nice arrangement of sampleable funk.

We drop the Otis Redding track sampled by Marley Marl for the old school classic “The Symphony” in the Crate Highlight portion of the show.

Other selections include: Blackbyrds, Poets Of Rhythm, the Visioneers, C.E.B., KRS-One, Shock G, Modeselektor, and Mad Cobra.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #50 10-20-2012
shows.description:
We go heavier with the funk in the first half, then kick into high-gear with the classic rap for the remainder of Show #50. Lots of remixes and a few Golden Era favorites. 

Black Sheep sets off the Crate Highlight, as we play two Easy Listening tracks that made up “Flavor of the Month.”

Other selections include: D-Nice, JJ Doom, MC Solaar, Junkyard Band, Alain Goraguer, Andy Loore and 1773.
tracks: Oh No (Feat. Nate Dogg And Pharoahe Monch)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #52 11-03-2012
shows.description:
In Show #52, we add in a little more recent hip hop to the mix, which still embodies that old-school esthetic. Naturally, we still hold it down with the classics –both hip hop and funkwise. 

At the minimum, we could spend an entire show devoted to songs that sampled the break in “Kissing My Love” by Bill Withers, but we give you a few choice tracks.

Other selections include: Busdriver, Kyo Itachi & Ruste Juxx, Relic, Spice 1, Jack Arel, William DeVaughn, Houston Person, and Presto.

shows.description:
It’s been a year since The Overweight Lover’s passing, so in Show #53, we drop a 20 minute set in honor of Heavy D. We also spin more funk than usual in this episode, as we keep things extra-upbeat and vivacious.

One original track, one track that sampled it. We play the song that was used to create “Warm It Up, Kane” in this show’s Crate Highlight.

Other selections include: Maestro Fresh Wes, Keith Murray, Sugar Bear, Burning Desire, Cymande, The Soulful Strings, and Bonobo.

shows.description:
We get you prepped for the new PJ Katz release “92 Renault Music” in Show #54. We also drop some early-90s remixes and ripe-for-the-sampling funk.

In the Crate Highlight department, we spin the hot original track that was sampled for “Liquid Swords” by the GZA.

Other selections include: Black Sheep, Rakim, Reggie Rockstone, Sweet Tee, Lee Dorsey, Motherlode, Odetta, Evil Needle, and Rawhead.

shows.description:
It’s another comprehensive profile on Classic Hip Hop and Funk, as Funky Corners #55 extends to near four hours in runtime. Golden Era rap, soul, instrumentals, beats, dancehall and rare groove are all on display for your listening gratification. 

We drop a double Crate Highlight with Aaron Neville’s “Hercules” and “People Make The World Go Round” by The Stylistics. 

Other selections include: DJ Frantic, INI, Brand Nubian, Bumpy Knuckles & Statik Selektah, Son Of Bazerk, Bootsy’s Rubber Band, Clutchy Hopkins, Intimate Strangers, Ramp, Boombaptist, Bostic Beats and Hands.

shows.description:
It’s a bounteous program once again, as Show #56 extends to 3hrs+ in length. In addition to funky music, Ethan Ullman calls in to discuss bread, jam, and pickles. Later in the show, Jaquam Bodden comes through to talk about hip hop, sports and growing up in the Bronx. 

We spotlight “Right Place, Wrong Time” by Dr. John in the Crate Highlight segment of the show.

Other selections include: DJ Jazzy Jeff, The Funky 4 + 1, Jurassic 5, KMD, Steady B, Black Heat, The Chosen Few, Pete Wilsher, DJ Vladim, and Hydroponic Sound System.

shows.description:
We drop some eclectic hip hop in show #57, along with a more abundant funk & beat assortment, PLUS the classic standards you love. T_Wheels also discusses his time DJing at a Caribbean club, using his best (worst?) Jamaican accent.

We bring you the Ripple track that was sampled for the Golden Era favorite “I Got It Made” in the Crate Highlight segment of the show.

Other selections include: David Axelrod, Joe Tex, Lafayette Afro Rock Band, Kyo Itachi & Ruste Juxx, Lil Dap, Slum Village, Coldcut, Wax Taylor, and PJ Katz.
tracks: Who Got Da Props (MW Smooth Mix)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #58 Holiday Special 12-14-2012
shows.description:
It’s the Holiday show! Santa arrives with a sleigh full of bass, beats, soul, and gangster rap to stuff under your big ol’ Christmas tree this season. 

As if you weren’t going to guess…  We do “Christmas In Hollis” as our Crate Highlight in this episode.

Other selections include: Daz Dillinger, Hard Rock Kev Brown, Necro, James Brown, Donny Hathaway, Papa Nucc, Kambir, and the Berlin Symphony Orchestra.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #59 Featuring Fatty & the One-Man Party 12-28-2012
shows.description:
Fatty and the One-Man Party are back in the building for Funky Corners #59. We get into a 3-man panel discussion on the greatest rap groups of all time, plus reminisce about Yo! MTV Raps. The One-Man Party also blesses us with a DJ/scratch set & D.A. Jay calls in to let us know what’s good in the proverbial hood. 

Do you know what Joe Cocker song was sampled in “California Love?” Find out in this episode’s Crate Highlight.

Other selections include: Boot Camp Clik, Busta Rhymes, Cypress Hill, Freestyle Fellowship, Fat Larry’s Band, Fred Wesley & The Horny Horns, Oliver Sain, and Funk Daddy.

(Talk Over) J Dilla Feat. Allan Barnes
(Talk Over) The Black On White Affair

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #60 01-04-2013
shows.description:
Due to an unexplained DJ crisis, T_Wheels comes through with another 4 hour show. The first two hours feature much funk/downtempo, as well as late 80s/early 90s rap, sans cursing. We get all rough & tumble wit’ it for the second half, dropping grimy hip hop and mucky dancehall. 

Antoine Duhamel features in our Crate Highlight, as we play the track Wu-Tang sampled for “Gravel Pit.”

Other selections include: Rayvon Supercat, Chi-Ali, M.O.P, Mic Geronimo, Erick Sermon, Cyril Neville, Isley Brothers, Rick James, Quantic Soul Orchestra, and Dyke & The Blazers.
tracks: Just Wanna Touch Her (Stoned Jazz Mix)
Louder Than A Bomb (JMJ Telephone Tap Groove)
How U Get A Record Deal
When You Are Who You Are

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #61 01-18-2013
shows.description:
We’re in a brand new studio for Show #61, and thus experiencing some growing pains. We still come live & direct with the instrumental beats, funk and hip hop. 

We spin a T_Wheels favorite for the Crate Highlight. aka “Easin’ In” by Edwin Starr.

Other selections include: PitchPerfect, Xperiment, Main Source, Private Investigators, Rodney O & Joe Cooley, Grant Green, Greyboy, Eddie Henderson, and The Mohawks.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #62 01-25-2013
shows.description:
We go big with early-90s rap in Funky Corners #62. There is also a sprinkle of funk throughout, and T_Wheels gives travel advisories for the local area.

For the Crate Highlight, we drop a Barry White beat. Notable samplers include Nice & Smooth, Boss, and Beastie Boys. 

Other selections include: Cozone, Brother Jack McDuff, Ohio Players, Stanley Turrentine, Company Flow, Rampage, Yaggfu Front, and Shades Of Brooklyn.
tracks: Players Balling (Players Doin' Their Own Thing)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #63 02-01-2013
shows.description:
We dole out the Dilla in Funky Corners #63, in honor of the annual “Beat*Shot Spins for Dilla” event in Albany, NY. We also throw in a touch of Happy Rap, mid-90s rap, and just plain rap-rap. 

Lou Donaldson was sampled by Dana Dane, De La Soul, and a Tribe Called Quest. Find out which track, in the Crate Highlight segment of the show.

Other selections include: The Chakachas, Kay Gees, Stevie Wonder, The Beatnuts, Oddisee, Showbiz & A.G., and Groove B. Chill.
tracks: I Still Live With My Moms

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #64 02-15-2014
shows.description:
It’s all about the mathematics in Show #64. Funky Corners times two.  247 minutes long, 62 tracks, 3 Wu-Tang songs, 2 artist tributes, 1 food-rap block. In this extendo-episode, we acknowledge the passing of jazz great Donald Byrd, as well as hardcore rapper Tim Dog and intersperse their tracks throughout the program. 

Crate Highlight #1 is a breakdown of the samples used in Pete Rock & C.L. Smooth’s “Straighten It Out”. For Crate Highlight #2, we do the same with Tim Dog’s “F**k Compton.” 

Other selections include: Brass Construction, The Budos Band, Funk Inc., The Temptations, Ammoncontact, Cru, Das EFX, Raw Breed, Redman, and T_Wheels’ favorite Special Ed track.
tracks: Change (Makes You Want To Hustle)/Think Twice (Special 12” Mix)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #65 02-22-2013
shows.description:
We do a little experimentation with song tempo on Show #65. The tracks were intended to be mostly around 70 BPMs or 120+ but we ended up going all over the place. 

In the Crate Highlight, we take “Talkin’ All That Jazz” by Stetsasonic and drop 4 tracks they sampled to create it. As a bonus, we also drop the first ever “Commercial Highlight” with a Kid ‘N Play Sprite ad. 

Other selections include: D-Nice, Eazy-E, ED O.G. & Da Bulldogs, Isaac Hayes, Orgone, and Jazzanova.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #66 Featuring Fatty, the One-Man Party, & Emcee Graffiti 03-08-2013
shows.description:
We have Fatty & the One-Man Party in the house for Show #66. Emcee Graffiti inadvertently arrives at the wrong time slot, but we convince him to stick around for a beatbox/scratch session with the One-Man Party. 

On the old-school Crate Highlight tip, we pull apart “Eric B Is President” and deliver not one, but SEVEN tracks that were sampled for its creation.

Other selections include: Chocolate Snow, The Chubukos, Gramatik, Real Live, Sadat X and double-shots of Black Moon and Showbiz & A.G.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #67 03-15-2013
shows.description:
We celebrate the St. Patrick’s Day holiday on Show #67 by dropping some Irish-themed rap. A.K.A. House Of Pain. We also manage to sneak a 20 minute hip hop-dancehall set in the mix. 

For the Crate Highlight, we keep with the Irish theme and break down the samples in the original & remix versions of “Jump Around.”

Other selections include: Faze-O, Les McCann, Intelligent Hoodlum, Mobb Deep, O.G.C.and Apollo.
tracks: A Who She Me Dun (Dynamik Duo Remix)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #68 03-22-2013
shows.description:
We mix up the late 80s/early 90s happy rap with more of the grittier 90s hip hop in Show #68 (with some 70s funk thrown in for good measure).

Spring has just sprung, and we pay tribute to the season by dropping “Spring Again” for our Crate Highlight. 

Other selections include: Atmosphere, Donald D, Finsta Bundy, Terminator X, B.T. Express, Chicago Gangsters, Duncan Lamont, and DJ Food.
tracks: What's Up Doc? (Can We Rock?) [K-Cut's Mad Master Remix]

Mama Gave Birth To The Soul Children

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #69 03-29-2013
shows.description:
We go lighter on the funk but heavier on the Golden Era hip hop in Show #69. We also world-premier a track from the Bedroom Plumber D.A. Jay, & keep the Jamaican vibe going with a mini ragga set.

The original B-Boy-staple “Super Sporm” by Captain Sky is the Crate Highlight and we detail a few tracks that sampled it, including BDP and Public Enemy. 

Other selections include:, Mad Lion, Juvenile Committee, Raekwon, Tuff Crew, Johnny Hammond, Kool & The Gang, and David Axelrod.
tracks: Ill At Will (Feat. Rasco, Planet Asia, D. Villa)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #70 Nautilus Tribute 04-12-2013
shows.description:
Show #70 is a very special Funky Corners. We devote the entire program to the seminal Bob James song “Nautilus” and the many tracks that sampled it. It wasn’t easy to consolidate the multitude of songs into just two hours, but we do our best to provide the most variety in sample-usage. 

Aside from the original track, other selections include: 2Pac, Big L, Channel Live, Da Phlayva, EPMD, Group Home, Jeru The Damaja, Kwite Def, King Sun, Legion Of D.U.M.E., Murs, Onyx, Run-D.M.C., and Ultramagnetic MC’s.
tracks: Me Against The World (Soul Power Remix)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #71 Featuring Fatty 04-19-2013
shows.description:
Show #71 marks two notable dates in Hip Hop history. It’s the 3 year anniversary of the passing of Guru, formally of Gang Starr, as well as the 19th anniversary of the debut release “Illmatic” by Nas. We also drop a world-premier D.A. Jay track and have Fatty in the studio, to boot. 

We do a double Gang Starr Crate Highlight, playing the original tracks used for “Skills” and “Mass Appeal.”

Other selections include: Roy Ayers, B.T. Express, Gwen McCrae, Roy Ayers, Black Moon, Boogie Monsters, Group Home, Redman, and Freddie Finger.
tracks: Marshall Applewhite (Feat. Giant Gorilla Dog Thing & Gorilla Tao)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #72 Featuring PJ Katz 04-26-2013
shows.description:
Show #72 features a 1 hour+ call-in session with producer extraordinaire PJ Katz. He discusses his new project “Ear Food Vol. 1”, as well as sampling ethics, originality in music, and what he was listening to at age 17.

We have the longest one-word-title Crate Highlight in Funky Corners history with the Yellowman track “Zungguzungguguzungguzeng.”

Other selections include: Boogie Down Productions, D-Nice, Grand Puba, The Nonce, Stetsasonic, Saul Williams, and MC Ren.
tracks: (With PJ Katz Talk Over) PJ Katz

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #73 Featuring Johnny Speed 05-03-2013
shows.description:
It’s James Brown’s birthday! The Godfather would have been 80 years old, and we do our best to represent for him Funky Corners style. We also pay tribute to Chris Kelly by playing not one, but two Kris Kross tracks. A first for the show. If that weren’t enough, Johnny Speed makes his first appearance on the show.

The Crate Highlight is devoted to James Brown, and we play you FOUR of his songs in which BDP sampled for the track “South Bronx.”

Other selections include: The Bamboos, Curtis Mayfield, Flavor Flav, Mack B. Dog, Professor Griff, and Kool Moe Dee.
tracks: Son Of Public Enemy (Flavor Whop Version)
Let A Woman Be A Woman, Let A Man Be A Man
Funky Drummer/ Get Up, Get Into It, Get Involved/ Get Up Offa That Thing/Unity (Interlude) [Feat. Afrika Bambaataa]

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #74 Featuring D.A. Jay 05-10-2013
shows.description:
D.A. Jay comes through to talk to us about his new album “Grateful.”  We (relatively easily) persuade him to bust a verse or two throughout the program. We also take a call from fellow CDB DJ and Dancehall Champion, Sir Walford.

In the Crate Highlight segment, we play a Herbie Hancock track which was sampled by both, Chi-Ali and 2Pac.

Other selections include: DJ Wally, Grand Puba, PJ Katz, Playdough and Heath McNeese, Ultramagnetic MC’s and Thirstin Howl III.
tracks: I Still Live With My Moms (Clean)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #75 Featuring Jordan Hill 05-17-2013
shows.description:
Special Guest Jordan Hill comes though the spot on Show #75. He discusses his current projects and we talk him into a little live drumming over some funk tracks. As usual, we keep things concrete with a steady dose of Golden Era jams. 

For the Crate Highlight, we reveal the two reggae joints that were sampled to create Special Ed’s “I’m the Magnificient.”

Other selections include: Jackson 5, Le Pamplemousse, Kruder & Dorfmeister, Jurassic 5, MC Shan, Naughty By Nature, Organized Konfusion, plus doubles of Def Jef and LL Cool J.
tracks: Remember Me (Sure Is Pure 12 Inch Mix)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #76 05-24-2013
shows.description:
We throw in a bunch of remixes and go heavy on the hip hop in Show #76. We also drop some underground rap and T_Wheels ponders MF Doom’s sampling techniques. 

Interested in the samples used to make “Scenario?” We’ve got you, in the Crate Highlight portion of this show.

Other selections include: El Michels Affair, Fred Wesley & The J.B.'s, Pearly Queen, D-Nice, Diamond D, Donald D, and Da Phlayva.
tracks: How I Could Just Kill A Man
Crumbs On The Table (Stimulated Dummies Mix)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #77 05-31-2013
shows.description:
It’s Show #77, and it’s also the 25th anniversary of the Boogie Down Productions album “By All Means Necessary.” We play a few cuts from that album, as well as hold things down with mostly early-90s hip hop for the majority of the show. 

We drop a double BDP Crate Highlight (with some minor difficulties), featuring the samples used for “I’m Still #1” and “My Philosophy.”

Other selections include: J-Scrilla, Vincent Geminiami, The Headhunters, Gerard Wilson, Grand Puba, Jungle Brothers, Lone Catalysts, Royal Flush, Groove B. Chill, and Jaz B Latin.
tracks: If You've Got It, You'll Get It

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #78 06-07-2013
shows.description:
We mix things up pretty well on Show #78, dividing the time between, funk, newer/90s hip hop, some local music, and a beat or two.

We use the blues track “Cold Feet” by Albert King in the Crate Highlight segment of the show. 

Other selections include: Fried Chicken, Ann Peebles, Tony Rubio, Phil Upchurch, Homeboy Sandman, Jemini The Gifted One, Keith Murray, Saafir, Sylk Smoov, Three 6 Mafia, and Pepe Deluxe.
tracks: Good Times/I'm A Ruff Ryder (Feat. Jadakiss)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #79 06-14-2013
shows.description:
Show #79 is the run-up to Father’s day. As such, we do what we can honor the occasion by digging through the crates for a little dad-themed hip hop and funk (very little). 

In keeping with the holiday, “Daddy Rich” is the Crate Highligiht in this week’s program. There’s also an impromptu “More Bouce” triple-play for that posterior, as well. 

Other selections include: Frank McDonald, The Professionals, Sam Reed Band, Blahzay Blahzay, Freestyle Fellowship, Godfather Don, Lex Boogie From The Bronx And Goldi Gold, and Nikki D.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #80 Summer Solstice Featuring Fatty & the One-Man Party 06-21-2013
shows.description:
It’s the first day of summer, 2013! Fatty & the One Man Party come through to chew the fat and play some summertime-themed music. T_Wheels also drops some solstice science and Marty makes comparisons between happy rap and your old wardrobe. 

We play a favorite Pharcyde sample, “Summer In The City” by Quincy Jones, during the Crate Highlight part of the show.

Other selections include: Blackbyrds, Ronnie Foster, Reki, Devin B, Moka Only, Rakim, Xzibit, plus doubles of Gang Starr and Dr. Dre.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #81 06-28-2013
shows.description:
We stick mostly to the hip hop in Show #81, but manage to sprinkle in a few funk cuts. A lot of mixing, and not a lot of the chatter.
	
Find out which James Brown track was sampled to create “How Kool Can One Blackman Be” and “Vapors,” in our Crate Highlight segment.

Other selections include: EC Illa, Jimmynort, Large Pro, N.W.A., Poor Righteous Teachers, A Tribe Called Quest, Bad Medicine, The Strange Fruit Project, and Curtis Mayfield.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #82 Wu 07-12-2013
shows.description:
Show #82 starts as normal, but at some point lands in the Island of Shaolin. Through numerous listener requests and deliberate campaigning, we end up devoting 58.82% of the show to Wu-Tang Clan-related music. 

We even re-do a special C.R.E.A.M. Crate Highlight from a past Funky Corners. 

Other selections include: James Brown, Kev Brown, Def Squad, K-Def, and Wu, Wu, Wu.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #83 07-19-2013
shows.description:
We drop mostly old school and underground hip hop in Show #83, but also manage to hit up a small funk set during the program. Comedian Ethan Ullman calls in and discusses his least favorite city in the Capital District and, unfortunately, talks about how bad it got when he had a kidney stone.

We spin a classic soul favorite in the Crate Highlight segment, which was sampled most famously by Prince Markie Dee and Grand Daddy I.U.

Other selections include: Akrobatik, Danger Doom, Diamond D, Goodword, Marco Polo, Kid Dynamite, Orgone and 24-Carat Black.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #84 07-26-2013
shows.description:
We’re back to the up-tempo business in Show #84. We drop some old school from the Happy-Rap era, along with an assortment of funk and some Gangsta thrown in. 

The Crate Highlight is a dance-party favorite, which was sampled by a wide range of artists including the Sugarhill Gang, MC Shan, Boss, and O.C.

Other selections include: 2Pac, Cypress Hill, Def Jef, Doug E. Fresh & The Get Fresh Crew, James Brown, Donald Byrd, Michael Jackson, and 100% Pure Poison.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #85 08-02-2013
shows.description:
We once again rewind some dancehall selections, and also continue with the classic hip hop in Show #85. There’s a small funk set plus we dip into a few obscure-errr rap tracks to top it all off. 

Crate Highlight features a Barry White standard. We play you a few notable songs which sampled it.   

Other selections include: The Extremities, Kool & The Gang, Sammy Nestico, Janne Schatter, Capleton, Big Shug, ED O.G. & Da Bulldogs, Kid Tsunami, L The Head Toucha, and X-Clan

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #86 Featuring D_Wheels 08-09-2013
shows.description:
We take it waay back to the Old School (even more so than usual) to celebrate hip hop’s 40th  anniversary, in Show #86. The Brothers Wheeler are reunited as T_Wheels’ brother D_Wheels slides into the spot to discuss the good ol’ days, play some early hip hop hop & talk plenty of nonsense. 

For the Crate Highlight, we keep with the roots of hip hop, and break down the samples & interpolations in Afrika Bambaata’s “Planet Rock.”

Other selections include: Blackbyrds, Soho, West Street Mob, Living Legends, N.W.A., O.G. Style, Yelawolf, and the Fat Boys.
tracks: Do You Know What Time It Is?
Eric B Is President (Todd Terry Remix)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #87 Featuring Kid Taiwan & D.A. Jay 08-16-2013
shows.description:
Returning guests D.A. Jay and Kid Taiwan descend upon the studio for a very special episode of Funky Corners. On Show #87, we talk about upcoming projects and highlight a number of D.A.Jay’s new & classic tracks. Kid Taiwan kicks some Chinese and tells us his feelings on international rap. The show also features multiple freestyle sessions, culminating with a ragga/beatbox/guitar extravaganza. 

We drop a Parliament funk staple for the Crate Highlight of the evening, which has been sampled by such artists as Ice Cube, King Tee, and Dr. Dre.

Other selections include: Big L, Biz Markie, De La Soul, Lucas, Masta Ace, The Nonce, and J-Live.

Unfortunately, due to U.S. restrictions, the full tracklist cannot be posted.
tracks: Say Hi To The Bad Guy

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #88 08-23-2013
shows.description:
It’s Show #88 and it’s also back to school time! We’re celebrating by playing the occasional “education-related” hip hop track. We also premier a D.A. Jay track that is literally only minutes old. 

We do “Schoolboy Crush” by the Average White Band for our Crate Highlight of the evening.

Other selections include: Leaders of the New School, Newcleus, Public Enemy, Raw Fusion, Spearhead, Kurtis Stanley, Ultramagnetic MCs, and more D.A. Jay.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #89 Featuring Fatty 08-30-2013
shows.description:
Fatty is in the house for Show #89, and he & T_Wheels make a pact to play more funk. It’s also the day after Michael Jackson’s birthday, but we struggle to find non-top 40 tracks to comply with WCDB restrictions.

We do up a Busta Rhymes/Seals & Crofts sample during the Crate Highlight portion of the program.

Other selections include: Black Rob, DJ Vladim, Eazy-E, Jeru The Damaja, Onyx, Poor Righteous Teachers, Prince Paul, Frankie Seay & The Soul Riders, James Polk And The Brothers, Ohio Players, and the Meters.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #90 Featuring One-Man Party 09-06-2013
shows.description:
We throw down an upbeat old school assortment in Funky Corners #90. The One-Man Party joins T_Wheels in the WCDB studio for a special guest DJ set. The fellas chat it up, plus drop one of the worst (best?) Tony D tracks ever. 

We do up a funky Aretha Franklin track for the Crate Highlight, sampled most famously by EPMD.

Selections include: K-Solo, Main Source, Non Phixion, Prime Minister Pete Nice & Daddy Rich, Public Enemy, Franz Auffray, Joe Bravo, Johnny Hammond, The Undisputed Truth, and Boombaptist.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #91 09-13-2013
shows.description:
The upbeat hip hop continues on Show #91. Starting with a little funk that gets entirely abandoned for classic rap the rest of the way. 

Featured in the Crate Highlight segment is a lesser-known James Brown track which was sampled for BDP’s “Poetry.”

Selections include: Above The Law, Billy Brooks, The Bar-Kays, Digital Underground, Dizzy Rascal, Doug E. Fresh & The Get Fresh Crew, Mad Skillz, Showbiz & A.G., and Pete Rock.
tracks: Doug E. Fresh & The Get Fresh Crew

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #92 Featuring B-Eazy & Fatty 09-20-2013
shows.description:
In the first half of Show #92, we are extremely fortunate to be joined by old-school rap-pioneer B-Eazy. We go back to Harlem World to recount his experiences growing up in a burgeoning hip hop culture. He discusses his musical projects, plus defines what it meant to have “Marshmallows” back in the day. Since the show runs nearly four hours in length, Fatty sticks around for the remaining two, to make sure T_Wheels keeps his wits.  

We deliver two Crate Highlights on this extended program. The first is the famed “Heaven & Hell...” by the 20th Century Steel Band and the second is the track that DJ Shadow sampled for “Organ Donor.” 

Selections include: Boss, Donald Byrd, Capital Tax, Cymande, Deltron 3030, Devin B, Dezmatic, Eric B. & Rakim, The Fatback Band, Funkadelic, Lords of the Underground, Mad Dukez and Fresh Kils, MC Lyte, Son of Bazerk, Terminator X, Twin Hype, and MC Paul Barman.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #93 09-27-2013
shows.description:
With some inspiration from WCDB’s own Soul Guru, The Nightowl, T_Wheels spreads the funk thick and heavy on Show #93. Also included is a choice selection of underground rap and some of the 90s artists you love.

Find out which JBs track was sampled by EPMD, Ice-T, and Run-D.M.C., in the Crate Highlight segment of the program.

Selections include: All The People, Oscar Brown Jr., D00d Computer & Sess Da Great, Dr. Octagon, Jeru, The Liquid Crystal Project, Lyrics Born, Curtis Mayfield, Nine, Raw Breed, Grover Washington Jr., and Deuces Wild.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #94 2-Year Anniversary All-Vinyl
shows.description:
Yes, Man! It’s the Funky Corners 2 Year Anniversary on WCDB! To keep tradition, we play straight wax from the crates. Strictly vinyl! Fatty, One-Man Party, Johnny Speed, Lo-Fi Lobo, and Oddy Gato join T_Wheels to get loose, Funky-Corners style. 

For the evening’s Crate Highlight we spin records that sampled the funk classic “The Payback,” by the Godfather of Soul. 

Selections include Big Pun, Peter Brown, Dennis Coffey and the Detroit Guitar Band, Gang Star, Heather B, The High & Mighty, Mass Production, Mr. Lif, Nas, Notorious B.I.G., Public Enemy, Erick Sermon, Zion I, and Jamal.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #95 10-11-2013
shows.description:
We mix it up with the funk, soul, beats and rap on Funky Corners #95. In this episode, we go heavier on the underground rap and bring in more of that 518 flavor, as well.

The original track that was sampled for 2Pac’s “All Eyez On Me” is revealed in the Crate Highlight portion of the program. 

Selections include: Das EFX, Del The Funky Homosapien, El Michels Affair, Group Home, GZA, Little Sister, M.O.P., Neso, Orgone, Shuggie Otis, The Phoenix Authority, and Rass Kass.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #96 10-18-2013
shows.description:
Funk rides in the backseat, as Hip Hop has its grip firmly placed on the steering wheel of Funky Corners #96. For the record, Dancehall is somewhere on the roof rack. 

We play the original track which was sampled by the Golden Era classic “I Got To Have It” by Ed O.G. & Da Bulldogs. Before he was simply “Edo” and dropped Da Bulldogs.  

Selections include: C.E.B., Ice Cube, MC Lyte, Mr. Chop, Populous, Shabba Ranks, W. Rockman, Rose Royce, Merl Saunders, Waajeed, plus a Cru double.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #97 11-01-2013
shows.description:
It’s Funky Corners #97 and we come through with the best in 90s rough hip hop. We get an assortment of listener requests, and T_Wheels talks about the best Halloween costume to come knockin’ at his door this year. 

In honor of the season, we revisit a past Crate Highlight and play the original track that made up the Geto Boys classic “Mind Playing Tricks on Me.”

Selections include: Black Star, The D.O.C., Eric B & Rakim, Funkdoobiest, Jedi Mind Tricks, Mad Skillz, Main Source, Mickey Erbe Orchestra, Oh No, Outkast, Parliament, Soul Tornadoes, and Kurious.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #98 11-08-2013
shows.description:
The selections are fast, and come furiously on Funky Corners #98. It’s chilly outside, but we keep it hot with the spicy rap and a bit of fiery funk, all with a bit of neo-soul-artsy seasoning for flavor. 

The Crate Highlight is a Cameo dance classic which was sampled by Brand Nubian, Heavy D, and the Jungle Brothers. Hint…it’s not “Word Up.”

Selections include: Banbarra, The Broken Keys, Big Daddy Kane, Company Flow, Gravediggaz, Just-Ice, Kool & The Gang, Maestro Fresh Wes, MC Serch, Moka Only, Newcleus, Oddisee, The Pharcyde, Soul Position, The UMC’s,The Ultramagnetic MC’s, and Flavor Flav.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #99 11-15-2013
shows.description:
We swing back into a better funk/rap ratio in Show #99. Also featured are some under-the-radar gems, remixes and off-center hip hop.

The original track that Showbiz & A.G. sampled for their old-school favorite “Party Groove,” is on display in the Crate Highlight segment of the program.

Selections include: The Afros, Against the Grain, Busdriver, Digital Underground, The Free Design, Freedom, Ghostface Killah, The Goats, Hippo, Kool G. Rap & DJ Polo, Masta Ace, Masta Killa, MC Ren, Curtis Mayfield, Nice & Smooth, Run D.M.C., The Wild Magnolias, Xzibit, and Zimbabwe Legit.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #100 11-22-2013
shows.description:
AaAARRaaAAGgHH   It’s Show #100 and apparently we celebrate by playing less happy rap and more of the tough-guy stuff. Included in the mix is a hit of rude-boy ragga, plus salty soul to blow your wig. 

It’s a West Coast-ish Crate Highlight as we play an original track that was sampled by Snoop and 2Pac (J-Live as well).

Selections include: Aceyalone, Roy Ayers, Donald Byrd, Barry Cooper, Doug E. Fresh, Marvin Gaye, KRS-One, Jurassic 5, Masta Ace, Public Enemy, Cutty Ranks, Super Cat, plus a world-premier from the Pig Food Records crew.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #101 11-29-2013
shows.description:
Back with more funky hip hop, T_Wheels is alone and a little off the rails. It’s the post-Thanksgiving show and there isn’t a soul on campus, apart from our fair host. As the heat in the studio is low, he keeps it sweltery with the pepped-up musical hotness.

Blood, Sweat & Tears is featured in the Crate Highlight segment of this week’s show. Run-D.M.C., Public Enemy, and 3rd Bass all took samples from it. 

Selections include: Biz Markie, Cash Money & Marvelous, Cypress Hill, Nice & Smooth, The Pharcyde, RJD2, Sly & The Family Stone, A Tribe Called Quest, Johnny “Guitar” Watson, and Skee-Lo.
tracks: Giant Gorilla Dog Thing, elsphinx, Benn Grimm, Grizzly Grimace, Alaska & Dizzo

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #102 12-06-2013
shows.description:
It didn’t take long for the “Return of the Happy Rap,” aka Funky Corners Show #102. However, listener requests prevent the show from going all Polkadelic for the full 2 hours. Also, T_Wheels has a case of mushmouth throughout, and learns the apparent technical realities of playing Positive K on-air.

We feature the track “Four Play,” which was sampled in Digital Underground’s “Packet Man,” and the Gang Starr track “Step in the Arena.” As usual, the Crate Highlight segment is half-way through the program.

Selections include: Black Sheep, Bronx River Parkway, Connie Price & The Keystones, Dabrye, First Platoon, Fu-Schnickens, Godfather Don, Redman, Erick Sermon, Smif-N-Wessun, Steady B, Step Brothers, and a triple “Before I Let Go” set.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #103 Holiday Special Featuring Raider's Hat 12-13-2013
shows.description:
Happy Holidays! It’s the annual Funky Corners Christmas/Hanukkah/Yule/Kwanzaa program. We can’t really pigeonhole our show into one religion, so consider it a “Celebration of the Season,” with WCDB’s very own Santa Claus-type figure, Raider’s Hat. We get down for the Holiday in every way you’d expect from Funky Corners.

We take a page from last year’s set list and kick the Clarence Carter track which Run-D.M.C. sampled for “Christmas in Hollis.” It just wouldn’t be the same without it!

Selections include: Bone-Thugs-N-Harmony, Dana Dane, Eazy-E, Electric Jungle, Hard Rock, Donny Hathaway, Jackson 5, Juice Crew, Moka Only, Mr. Lif, Papa Nucc, Scribbling Idiots, Shawn Lee’s Ping Pong Orchestra, and the Berlin Symphony Orchestra.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #104 Final Capital Coup Featuring Lo-Fi Lobo & Raider's Hat 01-10-2014
shows.description:
Funky Corners is back after a small winter hiatus. T_Wheels takes this opportunity to get back to the Funky Corners basics –Old School Hip Hop, Funk, & Beats. Additionally, it’s Lo-Fi Lobo’s last Capital Coup broadcast on WCDB, and we do our best to send him off real proper-like. 

We flip up the Crate Highlight, and play FIVE tracks 3rd Bass sampled for their classic “Steppin’ to the AM.”

Selections include: Dennis Coffey, Da Youngsta’s, Funk Inc., House of Pain, Jurassic 5, Kid ‘N Play, MF Doom, Naughty by Nature, Nightmares on Wax, Public Enemy, Showbiz & A.G., Slick Rick, Dr. Lonnie Smith, and Kurious.

(Talk with D.A. Jay Over) Dark Billy
Giant Gorilla Dog Thing, elsphinx, Benn Grimm, Alaska & Dizzo

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #105 Featuring PJ Katz & Fatty 01-17-2014
shows.description:
Funky Corners is pleased and honored to host producer, musician, and engineer, PJ Katz, on Show #105. His new album “Ear Food: Vol 2” has just been released and we give it the proper treatment. PJ not only discusses what went into the creation of this album, he actually shows us. Armed with his own turntable, Mr. Katz spins a selection of records that he sampled to create the latest Ear Food release. Joined by Fatty, he also talks to T_Wheels about his upcoming projects, live events, and the very special place he goes to preview his beats.

Unfortunately, due to U.S. restrictions, the full tracklist cannot be posted.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #107 01-31-2014
shows.description:
The theme is Slow and Low (or at least medium-tempo and moderate volume) for Funky Corners #107. Runnin’ the BPM in the mid-70, T_Wheels digs deep in the crates for a little bit of everything & anything to fit the bill. From West Coast rap, to Roots Reggae, back to instrumental funk, show #107 delivers the breadth of goods. 

We take a break from the norm and play a folk-rock Crate Highlight which was sampled by Biz Markie and Finsta Bundy.

Selections include: Blue Scholars, Ken Boothe, Ian Carr, Charles Heron & Vinny Knuckles, Collective Efforts, Geto Boys, Ghostface Killah, Grand Daddy I.U., Ice Cube, Ice-T, Joe Gibbs & The Professionals, Loadstone, Bill Near, Jimmy Ponder, Erick Sermon, Styles of Beyond, and Hardy’s Jet Band.
tracks: Let The Good Times Roll Pt. 1

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #108 Featuring D.A. Jay 02-07-2014
shows.description:
The homie D.A. Jay is back in the spot, and fired up with a brand new release. We get the lowdown on the Jamaican Sensation’s new music, new videos and other upcoming projects. He world-premiers four tracks from his latest album, plus gives us another freestyle session full of boogie and combustion. 

The Crate Highlight tonight is a Love Unlimited Orchestra track that Q-Tip sampled for the hit “Vivrant Thing.”

Selections include: 3rd Bass, Blackbyrds, D-Nice, Digital Underground, Divine Styler, Dynamic Corvettes, The Funk League, Fu-Schnickens, Grand Puba, Koushik, LL Cool J, and Young Black Teenagers.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #109 Valentine's Special Featuring Lady J (Virgomega) 02-14-2014
shows.description:
Happy Valentine’s Day! It’s that sugary, overly-hyped, commercial holiday full of obligation and unwanted advances. However, Funky Corners is feeling the love and we decided to bring you the best hip hop & funk the season has to offer. T_Wheels is joined in the studio by the Duchess herself, Lady J (aka Virgomega) for two hours of music so sweet, you’ll need a filling.

To get you in the mood, we lay out the provocative “Risin’ to the Top” for our Crate Affair of the evening. 

Selections include: Mary J. Blige, Bush Babees & Mos Def, Cash Money & Marvelous, Bootsy Collins, Gang Starr, The Isley Brothers, Leon Haywood, Judy Clay & William Bell, PJ Katz, Lee Fields & The Expressions, Mad Lion, Outkast, Tom Scott, Slick Rick, and J. Dilla.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #110 Featuring Jordan Hill 02-21-2014
shows.description:
We’re back in the triple-digit BPMs, which means a heavier dose of music from the Happy Rap era. The show culminates with a mini early-rap tribute and chat with Jordan Hill. 

A variety of artists sampled “Light My Fire” by Young-Holt Unlimited. We’ll play you three of them in the Crate Highlight segment. 

Selections include: Bronze Nazareth, Circle Of Power, D-Nice, Dee Felice Trio, Doug E. Fresh & The New Get Fresh Crew, The Jimmy Castor Bunch, Kool Moe Dee, Nice & Smooth, Poor Righteous Teachers, Scarface, Sly & The Family Stone, Stetsasonic, Threat, A Tribe Called Quest, and Chubb Rock.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #111 Featuring Jordan Hill 02-28-2014
shows.description:
In contrast to last week’s fast-paced episode, Funky Corners #111 is decidedly more laid-back tempo-wise. We keep it fresh with the Backpacker-style hip hop, along with some instrumental funk, plus a freestyle sesh with Jordan Hill. 

For our Crate Highlight, we dissect DJ Shadow’s “Midnight In A Perfect World,” and recount five songs that were sampled in its creation.

Selections include: Ahmad, Brand Nubian, Deltron 3030, Ghostface Killah, The Last Poets, Mickey & The Soul Generation, Mos Def, Onyx, Pancea, Peanut Butter Wolf, Prince Paul, Raw Fusion, Roy Ayers Ubiquity, War, and Quincy Jones.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #112 Featuring Jordan Hill 03-07-2014
shows.description:
Show  #112 starts precariously, primarily due to T_Wheels fracturing a needle during a Run-D.M.C. track. Fortunately, it’s a quick recovery and we’re back to the usual Funky Corners funky business. The Revolution Radio/Funky Corners mashup continues, as Jordan Hill returns to rap a bit, both literally and figuratively. 

We deliver a West Coast favorite for the Crate Highlight of the show; “Get Up To Get Down” by Brass Construction. 

Selections include: Big Pun, Chi-Ali, Cypress Hill, Diamond D & The Psychotic Neurotics, JB AKA Dirty Moses, King Hector & The Soul Dynamites, Nice & Smooth, Joe Quartermain, Clarence Reid, Shabazz The Disciple, Talib Kweli & Hi-Tek, Michael Wycoff, and Shyste Chronkyte.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #113 Featuring The One-Man Party 03-14-2014
shows.description:
Funky Corners welcomes the St. Patrick’s Day holiday with special guest, One-Man Party. T_Wheels pledges to play House Of Pain during the show, then proceeds to omit them from the program entirely.  

You like Eric B. & Rakim? Good, ‘cause we’re going to break down the samples used in “In The Ghetto,” including a special K-Def cover.

Selections include: Amp, The Beatnuts, Blahzay Blahzay, Dayton Sidewinders, Heavy D & The Boyz, Onyx, Outkast, People Under the Stairs, David Porter, Public Enemy, Rasputin’s Stash, Sylvia Striplin, Sweet Tee, and Ugly Duckling.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #114 03-21-2014
shows.description:
More of that 518 music is featured in Funky Corners #114. We also bring a measured quantity of Backpacker Rap, 70s funk, and songs to welcome in the vernal equinox. 

“Spring Ain’t Here” by the Pat Metheny Group is the Crate Highlight of the season. Listen in to find out which BDP track sampled it.

Selections include: David Axelrod, Beastie Boys, Biz Markie, Chi-Ali, Quelle Chris, Cymande, Dennis Coffey And The Detrot Guitar Band, El Gant, EPMD, Curtis Mayfield, Moka Only, Naughty By Nature, Nujabes, OC, Reggie Rockstone, Time Machine, A Tribe Called Quest, Bobby Womack, and Black Star.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #115 03-28-2014
shows.description:
Not that there is a “typical” Funky Corners show, but Show #115 might be a pseudo-prototype. The program features artsy hip hop, 90s grit, heavy funk, poppin’ jazz, beats, plus a touch of Upstate NY in the mix. 

Bob James is back! We serve up “Storm King” and drop some tracks that chopped it up, in the Crate Highlight department.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #116 04-04-2014
shows.description:
It’s the 36th Anniversary of WCDB! We celebrate by playing old school hip hop, funk, and beats (what did you expect?). Furthermore, Giant Gorilla Dog Thing has a new album. We pony up and give “Horse” a run, in Show #116.

“What Can You Bring Me” is the Crate Highlight of the program. Featured samplers consist of Craig G and A Tribe Called Quest.

Selections include: Biz Markie, Black Sheep, Brand Nubian, Deltron 3030, Fugees, Tommy Guerrero, GZA, Kaotic Style, Mad Skillz, Melaz, O.C., Ohio Players, Pete Rock, Quasimoto, Roots Manuva, Skipless, Yu, and The Detroit Sex Machines.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #117 Featuring Raider's Hat, Jordan Hill, and Lo-Fi Lobo 04-11-2014
shows.description:
You thought he was gone for good, but like a stubborn rash, Raider’s Hat has returned. He and T_Wheels kick it, talking about everything from bedbugs to playing the flute. Mercifully, Jordan Hill swings by to offset the madness and deliver a fresh birthday freestyle. If that weren’t enough, WCDB alum Lo-Fi Lobo calls in to speak his peace. 

We get smooth with the Crate Highlight, and play the original horn sample used in “Bucktown.” Yeah, that one.

Selections include: Artifacts, Blackalicious, Da Phlayva, DTMD, Johnny Jenkins, Jeru The Damaja, Kwest Tha Madd Lad, The Meters, Onyx, Showbiz & A.G., and Parliament.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #118 04-18-2014 Featuring Jordan Hill
shows.description:
We’re representing conscience rap in Funky Corners #118, along with a healthy dose of funky soul. Some classic hip hop is thrown in, plus a big chunk of instrumentals. Once again, Jordan checks in and rolls with T_Wheels through the last quarter of the show.

We take a break from the funk, and play an original blues cut in the Crate Highlight segment of the program. Amongst the artists that sampled it are Big Daddy Kane, EPMD, and Fugees.

Selections include: 1773, Boogie Monsters, Chocolate Snow, Herbie Flowers, Fred Wesley & The J.B.’s, Grieves, Headhunters, Talib Kweli, Love Unlimited Orchestra, Johnny Madwreck, Curtis Mayfield, Mr. J. Bedeiros, Nightmares On Wax, Jimmy Norman, RJD2, and J-Zone.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #119 Featuring Jordan Hill 04-25-2014
shows.description:
It’s back to the dancehall in Show #119. We start with a 20 minute ragga hip hop set, and from there move on to that Golden Era rap. Also featured are funk breaks, and a second dose of reggae in hour two. 

UMC’s, Sunz Of Man, and Mr. Serv-On all sampled our Crate Highlight of the program. Listen in to hear what we’ve got for ya. 

Selections include: Reuben Bell, Boogie Down Productions, Solomon Burke, Capleton, Cold Blood, De La Soul, The Devastation, Bajja Jedd, Mad Lion, Stephen Marley, Nine, Cutty Ranks, Special Ed, and Divine Styler.

Here I Am (Come And Take Me)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #120 05-02-2014
shows.description:
Funky Corners #120 gets off to a bit of a rocky start with technical, and wardrobe issues, but manages to get on track after a short time. The show is packed with instrumentals, thick funk, and choice early 90s hip hop. 

The Crate Highlight gets smoothed out with Bobby Caldwell’s easy classic “What You Won’t Do For Love.” Artists that sampled it include Kool G. Rap, Guru, DJ Jazzy Jeff, and 2Pac.

Selections include: Afrique, Tha Alkaholiks, Average White Band, Eric B. & Rakim, Jay Dee, Jurassic 5, Kan Kick, PJ Katz, Kool Moe Dee, Jack Mayborn, MF Doom, Roy Ayers Ubiquity, Skull Snaps, Souls Of Mischief, Time Machine, West Coast Rap All-Star, Willowy, Yaggfu Front, and Roger Roger Ensemble.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #121 Featuring The One-Man Party and Jordan Hill 05-09-2014
shows.description:
Marty the One-Man Party & Jordan Hill are once again on the set in Show #121. It’s Mother’s Day weekend 2014, and unfortunately the only thing T_Wheels has prepped for the occasion is a reserve of yo’ mama jokes. The One-Man Party jumps on the wheels for a scratch-mix set, and Jordan again blesses the mic with his lyrics of fury. 

The Crate Highlight features samples of a song that’s a cover of an earlier song. We’re talkin’ “While My Guitar Gently Weeps” by Jimmy Ponder.

Selections include: Blockhead, D-Nice, Lee Fields, Ghostface Killah, Grand Daddy I.U., Eddie Hazel, Kool & The Gang, KRS-One, Lords Of The Underground, Main Source, The Pharcyde, Run-D.M.C., Armand Van Helden, and Brian Bennett.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #122 Feat. Fatty, One-Man Party, Oddy Gato, JB, Lo-Fi Lobo, Masai, Grand Phee
shows.description:
Funky Corners is pleased to host the BeatShot Music crew, including Oddy Gato, JB, Masai, Grand Phee from We Stole The Show, and the return of Lo-Fi Lobo. The fellas world-premier Oddy’s posse cut “The Turns” and talk about the multitude of projects in the works. It’s a packed studio, as Fatty and The One-Man party join the fracas & lend T_Wheels a hand. Not to be missed.

We barely have time for a Crate Highlight, but manage to sneak in the samples which make up the Tribe classic “Check The Rhime”. 

Selections include: Black Moon, Daddy-O, DJ Format, Emperor Penguin, EPMD, K. Fleins Field, J-Live, Killa Beez, LL Cool J, Masta Ace, Ol’ Dirty Bastard, Ruthless Bastards, and Just-Ice.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #123 05-23-2014
shows.description:
We’re back to the low BPMs in Show #123. That being the case, we play a disproportionate amount of West Coast hip hop. Also included is a reggae set, and some funky jazz.

We go deep in the archives and bring out “Up On Cripple Creek,” for the Crate Highlight of the show. It was most famously sampled by Gang Starr and The Pharcyde. 

Selections include: Beastie Boys, Boogie Down Productions, Boogie Monsters, D.A. Jay, Dead Prez, Syd Dale, Del, Dr. Dre, Ice-T, The Lost Generation, Eugene McDaniels, Busta Rhymes, Max Romeo, RZA, Dr. Lonnie Smith, Special Ed, and Freddie.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #124 05-30-2014
shows.description:
Show #124 starts with a bit of jazzy funk then moves on to the underground hip hop. We transition into a selection of downtempo beats, then move forward, back in time, to Funky Corners’ bread & butter; old school hip hop.

On the jazzed-up funk tip, we bring you the Bobbi Humphrey in our Crate Highlight segment. It was most notoriously sampled for the Ice-T classic “New Jack Hustler.”

Selections include: 2Pac, Biz Markie, Blackalicious, Fatback Band, Donny Hathaway, Clutchy Hopkins, Thom Janusz, Kid Capri, Little Brother, Lone Catalysts, MC Shan, Moka Only, Mux Mool, Oddisee, Skinny Boys, Slick Rick, St. Germain, Steady B, and Eddie Henderson.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #125 06-06-2014
shows.description:
It’s the return of the classics, in Show #125. A whole backpack’s worth of Golden Era hip hop for your boombox (literally or metaphorically). Also featured is some sampled-from funk that will have you sayin’ “wait..I know that from somewhere…”  

It’s the 26th Anniversary of the iconic rap album “By All Means Necessary,” so we mess around with “I’m Still #1” during the Crate Highlight portion of the show.

Selections include: 3rd Bass, The Bamboos, Big Daddy Kane, C.E.B., Captain Sky, Lyn Collins, Giorgio, Gramatik, Instant Funk, Jimmy Castor Bunch, Jungle Brothers, Jurassic 5, Kool Moe Dee, Nas, Organized Konfusion, Special Ed, X-Clan, and Kurtis Blow.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #126 06-13-2014
shows.description:
We’re back at it, once again. T_Wheels delivers a show packed with early 90s hip hop, plus a few pseudo-new rap tracks, as well. We also throw in the standard funk goodness, and a couple ragga tracks for the dancehall heads.   

Redd Holt Unlimited delivers fat bass and dark piano for the show’s Crate Highlight. Check it, halfway through the program. 

Selections include: Bounty Killer, Bugseed, Damu The Fudgemunk, The Extremities, Gang Starr, Gravediggaz, Kool & The Gang, Kool Keith & Automator, Large Pro, Sven Libaek, Lone Catalysts, Lord Finesse & DJ Mike Smooth, Mad Cobra, Skull Snaps, The Spinners, Super Love Cee & Casnova Rud, A Tribe Called Quest, The Whatnauts, and Poor Righteous Teachers.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #127 06-20-2014
shows.description:
Show #127 starts off with funky/jazz/soul-type music then moves on to the moderately-newish hip hop. More old school in the mix, then the program wraps up with classic breakbeat soul.

The Crate Highlight necessitates 25% of the show, as we bring you some rap stuff that sampled Ronnie Laws’ (Laws’ses?) “Tidal Wave.” Arguably, most notorious in Black Moon’s “Who Got the Props?”.

Selections include: James Brown, Churchill, Ron Contour, Dayrye, Dinson, Charles Earland, El Gant, Immortal Technique, Lee Fields & The Expressions, Medeski, Martin & Wood, Fred Merrett And Friends, The Notorious B.I.G., Wilson Pickett, and Raekwon.

As hard as it is to believe, this is the first Crate Highlight in which we’ve featured Roy Ayers. We show you who sampled his 1973 track “Red, Black & Green.”

We set off Show #153 with a World-Premier track from D.A. Jay, then follow up with a mini ragga-hip hop set. We swing into the funk, then round off the first hour with a bit of underground rap.

shows.description:
It’s freezing and snowing in the better part of Upstate New York. To counterbalance the bleak meteorological outlook for the foreseeable future, we drop an extended sunny West Coast hip hop set in Show #154. We also supply the standard funk and beats that Funky Corners is known for.

shows.description:
Funky Corners 158 is a packed show, front to back. T_Wheels finally comes good with all his promises. He gets on all the music he’s been referring to recently, and then some. Plenty of new music, 518 hip hop, and the first-ever Funky Corners rap with rock set. 

One original, one sample. That’s how we’re doing the Crate Highlight this evening. It’s Nas and Joe Chambers. Tune in to find out what’s what. 
 
Selections include: BaaskaT, D.A. Jay, Dorothy Black, Brass Construction, Charles Bradley, Lefties Soul Connection, Nobody Likes a Racist, Smoothe Da Hustler, Young Malk and IB, Young Planet, and Leonard Nimoy.
tracks: Day After Tomorrow Cypher (Feat. Shyste, Chuck Lawless, Mic Lanny, Taizu, Dephyant, ES-AR, Emcee Graffiti, & Sway Savage)
Inner City Blues (Makes Me Wanna Holler)

DMC, Chuck D, PMD, MC Serch, Terminator X, DJ Eclipse & Big Ko

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #159 03-14-2015
shows.description:
In Show #159 we get back into the heavy funk, which has been somewhat missing in recent weeks. Also featured is a dose of underground hip hop along with a special WCDB interview with Common. 

“Big Sur Suite” by Johnny Hammond is featured in the Crate Highlight portion of the show. Listen in as we play 8 tracks that sampled it.

Selections include: Akrobatik, Antipop Chapeau, Consortium, Break, Blackbyrds, Casual, Dr. Dre, Gaturs, MC Eiht, The Moments, Mos Def, Musab, Minnie Riperton, Alan Parker, and Seven Seas.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #160 03-21-2015
shows.description:
For the first time in some time, we crack the 100 BPM barrier on Funky Corners. Mostly late 80s-early 90s hip hop, but also included is a gritty set of soundtrack-worthy funk.

We ooze out the funk for the Crate Highlight, featuring artists that sampled “Son Of Slide,” as recorded by Slade. Watch out for Vanilla Ice!

Selections include: BoomBaptist, Frankie Cutlass, Fred Williams & The Jewels Band, The Incredible Funk League, Leaders Of The New School, Lords Of The Underground, Main Source, Keith Mansfield, The Microphone Prince, Prince Paul, Busta Rhymes, Steady B, Visioneers, and Blue Monk.
tracks: More Than U Know (Feat. De La Soul)
Keep Your Eyes on the Prize
Pick up the Pieces One by One
Blue Funk (Feat. Violent Public Disorderaz & DJ Chaid)
Steam (Oh, Oh, Let Off Steam Mix 12”)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #161 Featuring DJ Illy 03-28-2015
shows.description:
It’s Show #161 and we are very pleased to welcome special guest, DJ Illy. Straight from Virginia Beach, Illy lives up to his name, and drops a sick 70 minute+ set featuring all that’s good from his neck of the woods. T_Wheels bookends the show and plays a touch of contemporary boom bap. 

Selections include: Big Sean, Action Bronson, The Doppelgangaz, GRiZ, Kid Ink, French Montana, Rapper Big Pooh, Prhyme, Reiza, Vic Spencer, Tiga, Kanye West, and Yelawolf.
tracks: To Me, To You (Feat. Jay Electronica)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #162 04-04-2015
shows.description:
It’s been 20 years since Eazy-E’s passing, so we put together a makeshift tribute in his honor. Also on the program is a bit of underground artsy hip hop, some funk and some underground artsy hip hop funk.

In keeping with the Eazy-E sentiment, we throw down 4 of his tracks plus, the samples which were used to create them. All in the Crate Highlight segment; half-way through the show.

Selections include: Binary Star, Eddie Bo, Boogaloo Combo, Chicago Gangsters, Commodores, Esbe, FreshNerd Of 100 Akres, GGDT, Ghostface Killah, Grand Puba, Ice-T, King Shi, Public Enemy, Moses Rockwell, Sol*Illaquists Of Sound Thrupence, X-Clan, and Eazy MF’n E.

Unfortunately, due to U.S. restrictions, the full tracklist cannot be posted.
tracks: Eazy-er Said Than Dunn (feat Dr. Dre)
Ball Of Confusion (That's What The World Is Today)
Terminator X Speaks With His Hands

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #163 04-11-2015
shows.description:
Show #163
We change the format up a bit in Show #163. The first quarter of the show is devoted to dancehall/reggae (including a D.A. Jay premier), the second quarter is all funk, and the remaining half is entirely dedicated to the Crate Highlight of the program. 

The Crate Highlight is from the group E-U and has had enough songs sample it to fill nearly an hour of Funky Corners. 

Selections include: Busy Bee, Dan The Automator, DJ Krush, Fat Larry’s Band, Funkadelic, Impact Allstars, Kilo, Kool & The Gang, Mad Lion, Powerhouse, Shabba Ranks, Steady B, Sugar Ray & Stranger D., Super Cat, Tenor Saw, The Wailing Souls, and the Boogie Boys.
tracks: Doug E. Fresh & The Get Fresh Crew

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #164 04-24-2015
shows.description:
The music comes hot and fast in Funky Corners #164. 80s rap, boogie instrumentals, and African-percussion inspired funk dominate the program.

We dissect the De La staple “Me, Myself and I” and play 4 songs sampled in its creation. Not least of all is the super-extended version of (Not Just) Knee Deep.

Selections include: Collective Efforts, The Dismaster, Edan, Faust & Shortee, Flevans, Freestyle Fellowship, Grandmaster Flash & Melle Mel, House OF Pain, Intelligent Hoodlum, Jungle Brothers, Nightmares On Wax, Organized Konfusion, Johnny Pate, The Roots, Yaggfu Front, and Bucky Johnson.
tracks: Open Your Eyes (Feat. The Merrick Park Baptist Gospel Choir)
Bboy Breakdown (You Got The Job Mix)
Get Ur Own (Feat. Shawn Haynes, Book Diamond, & Don Black)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #165 05-02-2015
shows.description:
We drop the hip hop Benjamin Button-style in Funky Corners #165; up-to-date early on, then progressing back in time to the classics, by the show’s end. Also interspersed is a variety of funk staples from the 60s to the 70s. 

The Crate Highlight is taken from the master of breakin’ funk, Dennis Coffey. It’s the track “Getting It On,” which was sampled by Ed O.G. & Da Bulldogs, Kid ‘N Play, and Public Enemy, just to name a few. 

Selections include: Arabian Prince, The Beginning Of The End, Big Daddy Kane, Billi Wells’ Outer Realm, James Brown, Busta Rhymes, Groove B. Chill, King Tee, Kinky, MCCRD, Monie Love, P.O.S., Roots Manuva, and Three Times Dope, The Treacherous Three, Tower Of Power, Twin Hype, Yak Ballz.
tracks: Put Your Hands Where My Eyes Can See (Abjo Refix) [Rough Version]
Dennis Coffey And The Detroit Guitar Band
Give It Up Or Turnit A Loose (Undubbed Unedited Version)
It’s Hard Being The Kane (Remix Radio Version)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #166 05-09-2015
shows.description:
Contrary to just about every show preceding it, T_Wheels drops any sort of preparation and freestyles the playlist on Show #166. The BPMs are pushed to an almost uncomfortable limit, and full credit is given to Jonny Jibbs for the craziness. 

Find out which Booker T track was sampled by The A.T.E.E.M., Big Daddy Kane, Chubb Rock, and Roxanne Shante, halfway through the show. 

Selections include: D.A. Jay, Dazz Band, De La Soul, DJ Format, DJ Shadow, The Gap Band, Vin Gordon And Cannonball Bryan, Mike Harland, LL Cool J, The Moontrane Conductors, Newcleus, Planet Patrol, Run-D.M.C., Angelo Tinsley, Twilight 22, The Upsetters, and Seatrain.
tracks: You Dropped A Bomb On Me
Play At Your Own Risk (12” Vocal Version)
Catch The Beat (Bibi’s Love Breakbeat Mix)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #167 05-16-2015
shows.description:
T_Wheels rolls through another Funky Corners, semi-on the fly. Featured are cuts from the new Shyste & Rob Viktum album, esoteric rap, and more African Rhythms, as evidenced by the track “African Rhythms.”

We’re feeling the spring heat and look to Roy Ayers for the Crate Hightlight. On deck for Show #167 is “Everybody Loves the Sunshine.”  

Selections include: Fonzworth Bentley, Depakote, DJ Krush & Toshinori Kondo, DJ Shadow, East Flatbush Project, El-P, elsphinx, FreshNerd of 100 Akres, Steve Grey, Isaac Hayes, Jay Dee, Jneiro Jarel, Lafayette Afro Rock Band, Boonie Mayfield, Oneness Of Juju, Pronoun, Quasimoto, Gil Scott-Heron, Joe Simon, Tower of Power, Melvin Van Peebles, and Dopehead.

What Does Your Soul Look Like (Part 4)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #168 05-23-2015
shows.description:
Wheels is back, and (sort of) fully-plans the show. The first half is sliced up between instrumental beats, Golden Era hip hop, and 70s funk. The second half of the program is almost exclusively devoted to the Crate Highlight.

As mentioned, we drop the unassuming Le Pamplemousse track “Gimmie What You Got,” and are able to fill a full hour with the hip hop that sampled it. 

Selections include: 3 Grand, Tha Alkaholiks, Big Daddy Kane, Boot Camp Clik, Eaze, Eminem, Geto Boys, GZA, J Rocc, Johnny Madwreck, Jurassic 5, K-9 Posse, Kato, Kil Emil, MC Shan, MEDL4, The Meters, Mista 93, Nas, Cyril Neville, Pete Rock, Playdough And Heath Mc Nease, Rakim, Redman, Sir Fresh & D.J. Critical, T.D.S. Mob, Tuff Crew, and Larry Robbins Sportstudio Band.
tracks: You Know My Steez (Feat. Guilty Simpson)
Waiting For The World To End
Rock Steady Pt. II (Feat. Lord Tariq & Peter Gunz)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #169 05-30-2015
shows.description:
The show opens with a brand new D.A. Jay track then rolls into a ragga hip hop set for the first quarter of the program. We round things out in the first hour with soundtrack-y jazz and instrumental beats. Hip hop runs the remainder of the program.. 

This week’s Crate Highlight is brought to you by Funk Inc. The samplers include Pete Rock, Big Mike, and Da Lench Mob.

Selections include: 7L And Esoteric, Amerigo Gazaway Of Gummy Soul, BADBADNOTGOOD, Brian Bennett, Chubb Rock, DJ Mighty Mi, DJ Vladim, The Doppelgangaz, Fatlip, Frenkiah, Funk Daddy, Funkmaster Flex And The Ghetto Celebs, Metanite, Money Mark, Omegasix, Shabba Ranks, Skipless, Sonakine, Steele, Take, A Tribe Called Quest, and the Eighties Ladies.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #170 Featuring DJ Johnny Juice Part 01 06-06-2015
shows.description:
Funky Corners is honored to host the legendary DJ Johnny Juice Rosado. In the first, of a three part series, we talk to Juice about his formative years in hip hop. Growing up in the Bronx and moving to Long Island, he discusses b-boying, graf writing and how he got into DJing. The segment ends with Juice flexing on the Wheels of Steel. The One-Man Party provides additional turntable support.

Selections Include: Black Moon, Chuck D, Cypress Hill, X-Vandals, and Kings of Pressure.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #170 Featuring DJ Johnny Juice Part 02 06-06-2015
shows.description:
In Part 2, Johnny Juice recounts his history with Public Enemy. We get an insider’s view on the crew, their production style and the politics of being involved with one of the most influential rap groups of all time. As a special treat, Juice recreates his “Rebel Without a Pause” scratch live in-studio. 

Selections include: James Brown, Public Enemy, and PJ Katz.
tracks: (Talk With Johnny Juice Over) PJ Katz

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #170 Featuring DJ Johnny Juice Part 03 06-06-2015
shows.description:
We bring things up-to-date in the final segment with with DJ Johnny Juice. He gives us his take on current rap artists, concept albums, corporatism in hip hop, as well as what he’s up to now. Juice has his fingers in many musical pies, and we get a taste. 

Selections include: PJ Katz, Son of Bazerk and No Self Control, and HiCoup.
tracks: (Talk With Johnny Juice Over) PJ Katz
Son Of Bazerk And No Self Control
Let Me Tell You Who I Am

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #171 06-13-2015
shows.description:
We preview cuts from the new elsphinx album entitled “Brain Cave Deluxe,” in Show #171. The show is also punctuated with an extended mid-80s rap set, and the absence of nearly any funk/soul.

We drop “On The Hill” for the Crate Highlight; sampled by Saukrates, The Kid Daytona, D.I.T.C., Pete Rock, and Puff Daddy.

Selections include: 85 Decibel Monks, Absolute, Boogie Belgique, Braille, Ice-T, Illus, LL Cool J, Boonie Mayfield, Planet Asia, Run – D.M.C., Shyste & Rob Viktum, Spoonie Gee, T La Rock, and Stetsasonic.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #172 06-20-2015
shows.description:
We come through with the funk, which has been absent in Funky Corners as of late. Also featured is a bit of conscious hip hop and a mini Gang Starr & crew set. 

The Crate Highlight features a creamy jazz song entitled “A Master Plan,” by jazz drummer Norman Connors. Tune in to get the lowdown. 

Selections include: Ab-Soul, Amable, Average White Baby Huey, Band, Blue Black, Digable Planets, Aretha Franklin, Gramatik, Al Green, Jneiro Jarel, Madlib, Prefuse 73, Eugene Record, SE1DavidE, Matthew Salesky, ThoTho, and A Tribe Called Quest.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #173 Featuring Jordan Hill & Nyjah 06-27-2015
shows.description:
Funky Corners always goes better with Jordan Hill, no? Well he’s back and he brought fellow WCDB DJ Nyjah with him. It’s a packed episode as drop an extended freestyle session, get into current events, and slap you with that funk. 

We dig into the library of the ever-sampled Parliament-Funkadelic and come up with “All Your Goodies Are Gone.” Featured samplers are Ghostface, Boss, Poison Clan, and Salt-N-Pepa.

Selections include: Bloodstone, Bones The Beat Head, DJ Vladim, El Michels Affair, Funkdoobiest, Grant Green, James Polk & The Brothers, Lord Finesse, Ohio Players, Pete Rock & C.L. Smooth, The Pharcyde, Ray, Goodman & Brown, and The Rhine Oaks.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #174 07-04-2015
shows.description:
Funky Corners #174 features an extended sample-based instrumental set of the hip hop/funk variety. We also bring the underground flavor in the second half of the program. 

The Crate Highlight is brought to you courtesy of Eddie Henderson. We bring “Inside You,” which was sampled by Homeliss Derilex, Souls Of Mischief, and Jay-Z, to name a few. 

Selections Include: Analog Brothers, Badbadnotgood, Benefit, The Boogie Monsters, Bostic Beats, Centz, Dabrye, Dilated Peoples, DJ Krush, J-Flexx, Third Person Lurkin, Noi2er, Rhthmatical, Romo, RZA, and Peace Orchestra.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #175 07-11-2015
shows.description:
Once again, it’s time for the BeatShot Music Festival. Funky Corners 175 features music from many of the artists performing, both local and national. 

The Crate Highlight is the 1979 track “Survival,” by Annette Peacock. BeatShot attendee J-Live sampled it for “Braggin’ Writes.” We’ll give you his, plus a few other versions in which it was used.

shows.name: Funky Corners #176 07-18-2015
shows.description:
Still high off of the previous week, T_Wheels once again presents more music from the artists featured in this year’s BeatShot Fest. Perhaps taking a more surprising turn, the last quarter of Show #176 features the first ever Funky Corners “Hip-House” set. Sorry. 

B.T. Express is a perennial Funky Corners favorite, and we bring “Do You Like It” for the Crate Highlight segment of the program. 

Selections include: Gino Dentie, DJ Red Alert, Hiroshi Fukumura, Illa J, Jungle Brothers, KC Flightt, Kool Kyle The Starchild, Magic Disco Machine, Queen Latifah, Salsoul, Special Ed, Twin Hype, Dexter Wansel, and We Stole The Show.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #177 Featuring Garden Of Eden 07-25-2015
shows.description:
We’re pleased to feature a guest set by Garden of Eden on Funky Corners 177. His esoteric collection features international rap, and dubwise beats. Not to be missed. 

The Crate Highlight is bypassed for the time being, as we let Garden of Eden take full control of your stereo. 

Selections include: 2Ruff, A Plus, Ammoncontact, Bulimic Org, DJ Muggs & Planet Asia, Frenic, Funkadelic, Godessa, Gramatik, Heltah Skeltah, Bob James, K-Def, Latryx, Leaders Of The New School, Low Profile, The Man Who Never Came Back, Maxnormal TV, MC Totally Rad & DJ F**k Are F**knRad, Redbong, Reverse Engineering, Tone Deaf Junkies, Twelve, Daniel Vangarde, and Tykoon Suit.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #178 Featuring LaFabrock 08-01-2015
shows.description:
Straight from France, LaFabrock steps up and delivers an abbreviated, but commanding guest set on Funky Corners 178. We also bring the soul back, and contribute an assortment of various rap flavors for any discerning palette. 

An appetizing plate of funk is served up for the Crate Highlight, in the form of “Rule Of Mind,” by 9th Creation.

Selections include: 3rd Bass, Black Knights, Black Moon, Blackbyrds, Brick, James Brown, Danger Doom, DJ Jazzy Jeff, Fashawn, Ronnie Foster, Gang Starr, King Tee, Kool & The Gang, Lord Finesse, Main Source, Idris Muhammed, OutKast, Red Black & Green, Run-D.M.C., Erick Sermon, Slick Rick, Socialistik, Special Ed, Tosca, Billy Wright, and Del The Funky Homosapien.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #179 08-08-2015
shows.description:
We wheel back the dancehall in FC #179, with an impromptu ragga set. Also featured are cuts from the brand new Giant Gorilla Dog Thing and Moka Only albums, respectively. 

To keep the theme going, we grab an original that GGDT sampled for their track “51860.” Also sampled by Diamond Shell, Big Father Hi-Top & The R.O.C., X-Raided, K-Rino, and some guy named Jay-Z. 

Selections include: Big Father Hi-Top & The R.O.C., Biz Markie, Brother Ali, Capleton, Centz, Frankie Cutlass, Diamond Shell, DJ Vladim, Esbe, Fat Joe, Fu-Schnickens, Fugees, Giant Gorilla Dog Thing, Jay-Z, Kurupt,Lady Of Rage, The Lyrics, Moka Only, Nine, Poor Righteous Teachers, Sean Price, Cutty Ranks, Sixtoo, and K-Rino.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #180 N.W.A. Tribute 08-15-2015
shows.description:
“Straight Outta Compton” has just been released in theaters, and thus it’s only sensible to assemble a tribute Funky Corners-style. We present 2 hours of music inspired by, related to, and sampled by the rap supergroup N.W.A.

Instead of one Crate Highlight, we throw in a few throughout the program, spotlighting some of N.W.A.’s more notable samples.  

Selections include: 2Pac, Above The Law, Arabian Prince, James Brown, C.P.O., The D.O.C., Dr. Dre, Eazy-E, Fila Fresh Crew, Funkadelic, H.W.A., Ice Cube, Isley Brothers, MC Ren, Roy Ayers Ubiquity, Snoop Doggy Dogg, Marva Whitney, Yella, and Ohio Players.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #181 Featuring LaFabrock 08-22-2015
shows.description:
It’s the return of the funk, and more importantly, the return of LaFabrock. He doubles his last output, and turns over a 30 minute set for the good of the Funky Corners cause.  

It’s a “Bad Tune” for the Crate Highlight. We play six tracks that sampled the 1971 Earth, Wind & Fire effort.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #182 Featuring Dee Jay Jonny Jibbs 08-29-2015
shows.description:
Funky Corners #182 is an up-tempo situation, punctuated by the long-awaited arrival of DeeJay Jonny Jibbs. He’s back with a 40+ minute set brimming with UK beats and American rap. 

Selections include: Adrenalin, AlgoRythmik, Azaxx, Boogie Belgique, Brand Nubian, DJ Day, Del The Funky Homosapien, Sage Francis, Giant Panda, Hieroglyphics, Kool Keith, KRS-One, Living Legends, Lyrics Born, MC Serch, Maestro Fresh Wes, Master Ace, Mista Grimm, Mr. Chop, Mr. Lif, Palov & Miskin, The Pharcyde, Nicolas Repac, Smoov-E, Tuff Crew, Ursula 1000, and Ugly Duckling.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #183 All Funk 09-05-2015
shows.description:
It’s nearing the end of summer, and to wind things down properly we present an all-soul/funk show. Two hours of preferential grooves and original samples. 

Instead of playing hip hop songs that sample soul tracks, we double-flip the Crate Highlight, and present funk versions of rap tracks. 

Selections include: Afrique, Gary Bartz, Breakout, Bat Britt, Clarence Wheeler & The Enforcers, The Delegation, El Michels Affair, Robert Jay, Lefties Soul Connection, Mr. Chop, People’s Choice, Pleasure, Markis Precise, J. Rawls, The Soul Lifters, Ted Coleman Band, Trama, Uncle Louie, Visioneers, and Sweet Charles.
tracks: (Talk Over) Daniel Janin & Jean Claude Perric

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #184 Featuring LaFabrock 09-12-2015
shows.description:
The first quarter of show #184 features mostly instrumentals, including chopped beats and temperamental soundtrack-jazz-type-stuff. LaFabrock later infiltrates the proceedings and gives us a bass-heavy rap and beats set. We top it all off with an extended Crate Highlight. 

Roy Ayers brings US “Sensitize,” and we bring YOU 10 tracks that sampled it.

Selections include: 7L & Esoteric, Ab-Soul, Big K.R.I.T., Black Rob, Bornze Nazareth, Dennis Brown, Cap1, Crime Fam, Disiz, DJ Racy A.J., Grand Agent, Guts, Jeru The Damaja, Kisszanto, MC Eiht, Franco Micalizzi, Hudson Mohawke, O.C., Jay Rock, Rustie, Eric Ryan, Slim Thug, SomehowArt, Statik Selektah, Tobacco, Twisted Angels, Les Vikings, and Junglep***y.

Shaolin Monk vs Shadow Boxing Kung Fu
Life Story (Feat. Cheryl Pepsi Riley & Racquel)

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #185 Featuring DJ Illy 09-19-2015
shows.description:
Our homie from The VA, DJ Illy, contributes an astounding 70+ minute set on Funky Corners #185. He touches upon everything from 90s rap, to dancehall, all the way to a selection of contemporary hip hop.

Selections include: 50 Cent, Lloyd Banks, Beenie Man, Black Rob, Boogie Monsters, Busta Rhymes, Camp Lo, Channel Live, J. Cole, Common, Dead Prez, The Diplomates, Dr. Dre, Drake, Eazy-E, Fetty Wap, Future, GZA, Hellnote, Ice Cube, Talib Kweli, M.O.P., Meek Mill, Mr. Vegas, Outkast, Queen Latifah, Raekwon, Cutty Ranks, Red Rat, Shawty Lo, Snoop Dogg, Speaker Knockerz, Special Ed, Styles P, Trae, Ying Yang Twins, and Organized Konfusion.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #186 09-26-2015
shows.description:
The first hour of Funky Corners 186 is “underground newish-type rap music,” culminating with a mini-Upstate set. We do manage to fit the funk back, and blend something real sweet later in the program.

The Godfather is back for another Crate Highlight. We drop “Never Can Say Goodbye” by James Brown, along with seven cuts in which it was sampled.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #733 Featuring G-Spot from Pots & Pans Radio "The Secret Recipe" 03-20-2026
shows.description:
G-Spot is back on Funky Corners, delivering an incredible display of turntable skill that blurs the line between re-mix and re-ality called “The Secret Recipe.” Each track is meticulously reconstructed using nothing but the original samples. You’d swear it’s the original instrumentals, but it’s G-Spot building the tracks piece by piece with two turntables and a looping function. The amount of detail is next-level and may require multiple listens to sink in properly. And also, T_Wheels is somewhere on the show.

shows.name: Funky Corners Show #766 15th Anniversary Show Extra - 10 Hours of Beats
shows.description:
It’s a special bonus episode from the Funky Corners 15th Anniversary!

Notes from T_Wheels:
“I wanted to have music to talk over for the anniversary show without worrying about mixing live or repeating tracks on loop. This mix was intended to be 1 to 2 hours long, but every time I had a little bit of free time I would add on an extra 15 or 20 minutes. Eventually it got out of hand. For fear of it turning into the Winchester House of DJ sets, I had to cap it when it hit double digits. It's absurd and ridiculous and I'm not sure what you can do with it, but here is a 10 hour mix of mid-tempo instrumentals including rap dubs, acid jazz, Lo-Fi, glitches & scratches. No curse words or talking - just beats, ad-libs, samples, and the occasional chorus.”
